messages:
sam: Morning — following up on the RFC about our multi-region strategy. We need a recommendation: active/active with geo-routing vs active/passive failover for EU data residency + low-latency global reads. TL;DR constraints: EU customer data must not leave EU; some models are US-only due to licensing. Thoughts? @priya @li

priya: For EU residency we can't replicate PII outside the region. Option A: regional silos (active/active) with per-region DB and model cache. Pros: low latency, local compliance. Cons: hard to keep stateful features (session state, KV) consistent across regions. :thinking:

li: If we silo, control plane can be global but metadata must be stored separately. Keep model weights in a registry with region tags; runtime only pulls region-allowed models. Example routing policy snippet:

```
routing:
  - if request.user.region == "eu": region_preference: eu; allowed_models: [redwood-rlhf-eu, open-llama-q4_eu]
  - else: region_preference: nearest
```

ev an: Active/active with async replication + CRDTs for some non-sensitive state could work, but cost + complexity are high. Also: deterministic fallback if EU model not available -> fallback to smaller EU-compliant model, never to a US-hosted model. :warning:

sam: What about KV cache + prefix caching? If we replicate asynchronously, cold-starts in the DR region will be painful for latency-sensitive flows.

priya: We can split hot KV (region-local, not replicated) vs cold state (replicated, encrypted, and subject to residency filters). Use eviction policies that are region-aware.

li: Networking and telemetry: keep egress minimal. Audit logs that include sensitive markers must remain in-region and never be forwarded. Likely need region-aware log sinks and retention policies.

ev an: Testing and runbooks: recommend quarterly DR drills. Canary plan: shift 1% traffic to eu->us fallback and measure latency + quality delta. Key metrics: failover_latency_p50/p95, model_fallback_rate, residency_violations. I'll draft dashboards for those.

sam: Cost tradeoff — active/active increases serving fleet size (effectively N regions * baseline). For high-throughput enterprise customers that's OK. For small customers default to active/passive with ~30s RTO.

priya: Policy suggestion: default to regional-silo active/active for regulated customers; default customers get active/passive with upgrade path to active/active (fits Hosted vs Dedicated tiers).

li: Note on Private deployments (VPC/on-prem): simpler for residency — data never leaves. Still need a consistent admin UX and same model tagging semantics.

ev an: I'll open an RFC follow-up with rollout + testing plan and owners. +1 on per-region model registry tags.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: infra-tests/regional-routing -> started 1767892000 by evan

sam: Thanks. @priya @li please call out any missing edge cases (e.g., GDPR subject requests across regions). :thumbsup:

priya: GDPR edge: cross-region blobs must be deletable from remote replicas within SLA. Need a region-aware purge API and audit trail.

li: Another edge: model fine-tuning outputs that reference customer data — ensure fine-tune artifacts only stored in-region and training logs scrubbed.

ev an: Cool — I'll assign owners and timeline in the RFC and include the canary/playbook. End.
